title: ServiceNow SAM — Request Fulfillment & License Reclamation Workflow
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (ServiceNow SAM/ITAM workflow design: intake, fulfillment, entitlement, reclamation; platform-specific, multi-stakeholder).
Non-Microsoft platform; ServiceNow SAM module specifics are deferred to ServiceNow's official docs (don't invent).
hook: Run software requests and reclamation as a clean ServiceNow workflow
problem: When software requests live in email and reclamation never happens, the service desk drowns and licenses leak. This solution designs a repeatable ServiceNow SAM workflow for the full request lifecycle — intake and triage, entitlement and fulfillment, and automated reclamation of unused licenses — with the catalog items, workflows, and reporting that turn license operations into a measured, auditable process.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the ServiceNow SAM/ITAM model, the request lifecycle (intake → triage → entitlement → fulfillment → reclamation), catalog items and workflows, and reporting.

Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (a ServiceNow instance with SAM/ITAM, entitlement/CMDB data, discovery integration, roles and approvals) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing. ServiceNow-specific configuration is deferred to ServiceNow's documentation.

Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: define the catalog items and intake, build triage and fulfillment workflows, wire entitlement and reclamation, set reporting and KPIs, then pilot, validate, and expand.

5 PowerShell/integration scripts — request/entitlement discovery helper, fulfillment-data validation, a request and reclamation report, safe remediation of stale entitlements, and a scope/assignment helper. (ServiceNow data via the Table API where available.)
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for the assign-once, repeat-everywhere model.
short: Design a repeatable ServiceNow SAM workflow for the full request lifecycle — intake and triage, entitlement and fulfillment, and automated reclamation — with the catalog items, workflows, and reporting that make license operations measured and auditable. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
